item.title: Matthew Stafford throws four touchdowns as Rams rout Giants
item.description: Matthew Stafford threw for 327 yards and four touchdowns in the Rams' 28-6 win over the Giants, moving into sixth place in NFL history with 427 career touchdown passes. New York quarterback Jaxson Dart left with a suspected sprained MCL.

item.title: Brewers set a franchise record with their 98th win
item.description: Milwaukee blanked Baltimore 3-0 to complete a sweep and set a franchise record with 98 victories. Six relievers preserved the shutout after Jacob Misiorowski worked three scoreless innings, and the Brewers moved two games ahead of the Dodgers for the National League's best record.

item.title: Brighton hands Arsenal its heaviest defeat in three years
item.description: Brighton ended Arsenal's perfect Premier League start with a 3-0 victory, the Gunners' heaviest loss in three years. Pascal Gross, Charalampos Kostoulas and Chema Andrés scored as Brighton climbed to third, level with Arsenal and Manchester City on 12 points.

item.title: Dak Prescott becomes Cowboys' career touchdown-pass leader
item.description: Dak Prescott threw four touchdown passes in Dallas' 37-20 win over Washington, passing Tony Romo's franchise record of 248. The victory was clouded by Commanders rookie quarterback Jayden Daniels suffering a dislocated left elbow.

item.title: Ole Miss climbs to No. 4 after beating LSU
item.description: Ole Miss moved to No. 4 in the AP Top 25 after a 32-24 victory over LSU, reaching the September top five for a third straight season. The SEC placed 10 teams in the ranking, while Texas A&M plunged from No. 9 to No. 23 after losing at home to unranked Kentucky.

item.title: J.J. Spaun answers Presidents Cup snub with BMW PGA win
item.description: J.J. Spaun birdied four of his last five holes, closed with a 67 and won the BMW PGA Championship by two shots over a group including Rory McIlroy and Adam Scott. Spaun said being passed over for a U.S. Presidents Cup captain's pick supplied extra motivation.

item.title: Czech Republic rallies to eliminate the U.S. from Davis Cup
item.description: A day after the teams split the opening singles, the Czech Republic erased a 2-1 deficit by winning both reverse singles in Prague. Jiri Lehecka beat Learner Tien and Jakub Mensik defeated Ben Shelton to eliminate the United States 3-2 and advance to November's quarterfinals in Bologna.

item.title: Coventry earns its first Premier League win in 25 years
item.description: Jay Dasilva's second-half goal gave Coventry City a 1-0 victory at Nottingham Forest, the club's first Premier League win since 2001. A late Forest equalizer was overturned by VAR, lifting Frank Lampard's promoted side off the bottom after four straight losses.

item.title: Diamondbacks walk off the Yankees on a World Series anniversary
item.description: On the 25th anniversary of Arizona's 2001 World Series win over New York, pinch hitter Pavin Smith hit a two-run homer in the ninth for a 5-3 victory. The Diamondbacks ended a three-game skid and kept their faint NL wild-card hopes alive with seven games left.

item.title: Braves clinch postseason berth with three two-run homers
item.description: Atlanta secured a playoff spot by beating Houston 6-2 behind two-run homers from Michael Harris II, Ronald Acuña Jr. and Matt Olson. Tyler Mahle supplied a strong start, and the Braves cut their magic number for the NL East title to three.

item.title: U.S. and Czech Republic split opening Davis Cup singles
item.description: The United States ended the first day of its Davis Cup qualifier in Prague tied 1-1 with the Czech Republic. Learner Tien beat Jakub Mensik before Jiri Lehecka defeated U.S. Open finalist Ben Shelton in straight sets, leaving Saturday's doubles and reverse singles to decide the tie.

item.title: England recalls Alexander-Arnold and Palmer for Nations League
item.description: Thomas Tuchel recalled Trent Alexander-Arnold and Cole Palmer among 10 changes to England's first squad since the World Cup. England opens Nations League play against world champion Spain at Wembley on September 26 as Tuchel begins building toward a home Euro 2028.

item.title: Dodgers clinch 13th NL West title in 14 seasons
item.description: The Dodgers beat Cincinnati 8-2 to secure their fifth straight division crown and 13th NL West title in 14 years. Kyle Tucker went 4-for-5 with a homer, two doubles and three RBIs as Los Angeles improved to 93-60 and kept its postseason push rolling.

item.title: Pochettino turns to youth for U.S. men's friendlies
item.description: U.S. coach Mauricio Pochettino named a 28-man roster with 13 uncapped players for friendlies against Peru, Chile, Mexico and Canada, beginning the next World Cup cycle with a sharp turn toward youth. The group includes 16-year-old Cavan Sullivan, while Christian Pulisic and Folarin Balogun were left out.

item.title: WTA Finals will move to Charlotte in 2027
item.description: The season-ending WTA Finals will move to Charlotte's Spectrum Center in 2027 for at least three years. The tour plans to operate the event directly and pair it with a fan festival, aiming to turn its showcase for the top eight singles players and doubles teams into a signature women's sports event.
